1.pericope_label: Hear this word, ye kine of Bashan, that are in the mountain of Samaria, which oppress the poor, which crush the needy, which say to their masters, Bring, and let us drink. The Lord God hath sworn by his holiness, that, lo, the days shall come upon you, that he will take you away with hooks, and your posterity with fishhooks.

schools.summary: Read the epithet from geography and gender: the feminine forms mark the luxurious women of Samaria, and the rich pasture east of the river supplies the figure of cattle fattened for slaughter.
Take the great men as the target, named for effeminacy and perhaps for the calves they worshipped, and hear in the epithet the prophet's refusal to reckon their wealth as anything but fatness.
Keep the address open as to sex, iniquitous and idle drones either way, and press the herdsman's own trade for the point that fatted beasts are led out to slaughter.
Works the herdsman's dialect hardest, on cattle grown wanton on fat pasture that break the fences and gore the weaker of the herd.

debates.question: Who are the kine of Bashan?

positions.position: The luxurious women of fashion in Samaria, who address their husbands as masters and call for drink paid out of the robbery of the poor; the alternative that the feminines are sarcastic epithets for effeminate men is not a probable explanation.
The great men of the kingdom, named for their effeminacy, the rabbinic identification with the wives of kings and princes reported but not adopted.
Either, the iniquitous and idle drones whether men or women.
Two kinds of fishing, the rod and baited hook for small fish and the gaff for large ones, matched to common people and to the powerful.

The suddenness and irresistible character of a seizure that carries off men in fancied security; the imagery has seemed strange, and one translator renders instead that they shall be driven among thorn bushes.
The instrument is named outright, the Assyrian army, and the sentence extends to the children of the oppressors.

outliers.claim: Quarrels with the chapter division itself: whoever made it cannot have considered the argument, since the prophet is still reproving the rich men he had been threatening before.

themes: Hear this word, ye kine of Bashan, that are in the mountain of Samaria, which oppress the poor, which crush the needy, which say to their masters, Bring, and let us drink.
The Lord God hath sworn by his holiness, that, lo, the days shall come upon you, that he will take you away with hooks, and your posterity with fishhooks.

3.pericope_label: And ye shall go out at the breaches, every cow at that which is before her; and ye shall cast them into the palace, saith the Lord. Come to Beth–el, and transgress; at Gilgal multiply transgression; and bring your sacrifices every morning, and your tithes after three years: And offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, and proclaim and publish the free offerings: for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord God.

schools.summary: Press the Hebrew hard and admit where it defeats them, preferring emendation to guess-work, and read the ironical liturgy for the sarcasm the English loses.
Take the breaches literally and find a symmetry in them, and draw from the irony the doctrine that laboured worship at false shrines multiplies the offence.
Keep the fishing metaphor running through the breaches and turn the irony on the place, giving the people over as incorrigible.

debates.question: How is the going out at the breaches to be read?

positions.position: The fishing figure continues: the women tear the net by their flouncing and are taken out at those very tears, the city being the net.
Literally, and with a symmetry: those who broke the fences of law and justice find their own walls broken and are glad to escape with their lives.
Each one straight before her, women going tamely out through the breaches into captivity.
Headed in one line as judgment continuing because Israel would not leave its idolatry.

debates.question: Was the leaven in the thank-offering lawful?

positions.position: Never allowed in a sacrifice made by fire, so the prophet ironically calls on them to break a law he knew they habitually broke.
Against the express law, with a dare attached: do so at your peril and see whether it ends well.
Forbidden in one kind of offering but ordered with the thanksgiving, so the clause is lawful in itself and ironically commanded only because it is offered to idols.
Every three days, since the law required a tithe only every third year, the prophet lashing them with hyperbole for excessive generosity to base priests.
The three years stand, and the law that appointed them is cited.

outliers.claim: Declines the philology and keeps to the tone, holding that the prophet still refuses to count these pompous masters as men, which is the more pointed because the rich observe their ranks so strictly and are so hard to approach.

themes: And ye shall go out at the breaches, every cow at that which is before her; and ye shall cast them into the palace, saith the Lord.
Come to Beth–el, and transgress; at Gilgal multiply transgression; and bring your sacrifices every morning, and your tithes after three years:
And offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, and proclaim and publish the free offerings: for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord God.

6.pericope_label: And I also have given you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and want of bread in all your places: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord. And also I have withholden the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest: and I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city: one piece was rained upon, and the piece whereupon it rained not withered. So two or three cities wandered unto one city, to drink water; but they were not satisfied: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.

schools.summary: Read the famine from the poetic parallelism and the law's own threats, and hear the refrain as the Lord grieving over the failure of his disciplinary treatment.
Date the drought to an earlier reign, rule out the siege famine on the scope of the words, and explain why the drought is recorded apart from the famine it caused.
Turn the phrase into irony, fix the season from an old authority, and make the unequal rain a sign the people were meant to read.
Counts the five repetitions of the refrain and draws four things from them about the design of every rebuke.

positions.position: Not the siege famine in Samaria, confined to one city and a short time while this was in all the cities, but the seven-year famine a later prophet foretold.
That identification is reported, but the famine described by another of the twelve is likelier.

debates.question: Why did the wandering cities find no water?

positions.position: The fountains could have supplied their own people but were exhausted once such a multitude flowed in from every quarter.
Those who had water either had not enough or dared not part with it.

outliers.claim: Reads out of the fivefold refrain that God took it unkindly to be forced into doing what he did so unwillingly, since it is no pleasure to the Almighty to afflict.
Gives the physical picture behind cleanness of teeth: clean sharp teeth projecting from thin lips, one of the ghastly aspects of famine.

themes: And I also have given you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and want of bread in all your places: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.

And also I have withholden the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest: and I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city: one piece was rained upon, and the piece whereupon it rained not withered.
So two or three cities wandered unto one city, to drink water; but they were not satisfied: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.

9.pericope_label: I have smitten you with blasting and mildew: when your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees increased, the palmerworm devoured them: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord. I have sent among you the pestilence after the manner of Egypt: your young men have I slain with the sword, and have taken away your horses; and I have made the stink of your camps to come up unto your nostrils: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord. I have overthrown some of you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and ye were as a firebrand plucked out of the burning: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.

schools.summary: Read the blights as agricultural fact, correcting the rendering where the Hebrew carries a force the English blunts, and trace the ascent from smaller chastisements to greater.
Canvass the possible referents without settling them, and draw the theological weight of the accumulated strokes: remedies cannot reach men past recovery.
Anchor the pestilence in a known siege and insist that both the judgment and the deliverance were evidently from God.

debates.question: What is the pestilence after the manner of Egypt?

positions.position: Three readings are canvassed without decision: like the plague that took the firstborn; on the wilderness road, following the Targum; or sent on them as they travelled down for help and food during the famine.
The Syrian siege of Samaria, when an ass's head sold for eighty pieces of silver and mothers ate their children, relieved by the unseen slaughter of the besiegers.

The marginal rendering is preferred, with the captivity of your horses; Egypt is the birthplace of the plague, and the prophet is explaining its cause, hosts of slaughtered warriors left across the camp.
The plain sense: the riders killed and the slaughter so great that too few remained to bury the dead.
Only the close pairing of pestilence with the sword is noted.

debates.question: How far does the overthrow like Sodom extend?

positions.position: Narrowly, of particular houses or persons struck by lightning rather than whole cities burnt.
A distinct calamity, an earthquake and perhaps a volcanic eruption, supported by a long series of such shocks in that land from the fourth century to the twelfth.
The utter confusion of the state, Israel pulled out only as a brand is pulled from the burning.

outliers.claim: Makes the sequence itself the argument: one punishment leaves men guilty enough, but when God tries one way after another and still effects nothing, those who remain stupid under the accumulation are past recovery.

themes: I have smitten you with blasting and mildew: when your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees increased, the palmerworm devoured them: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.

I have sent among you the pestilence after the manner of Egypt: your young men have I slain with the sword, and have taken away your horses; and I have made the stink of your camps to come up unto your nostrils: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.
I have overthrown some of you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and ye were as a firebrand plucked out of the burning: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.

12.pericope_label: Therefore thus will I do unto thee, O Israel: and because I will do this unto thee, prepare to meet thy God, O Israel. For, lo, he that formeth the mountains, and createth the wind, and declareth unto man what is his thought, that maketh the morning darkness, and treadeth upon the high places of the earth, The Lord, The God of hosts, is his name.

schools.summary: Rule out any backward glance in the threat on grammatical grounds and make the reticence itself the point: having said what he will do, He is silent as to what He will do.
Refuse to choose between the ironical and the serious sense of the summons, and read the closing doxology as a device to rouse torpid minds.
Take the summons as a military challenge and end on the threefold name, warning that the verse has been painfully misapplied.

debates.question: Is prepare to meet thy God irony or a call to repentance?

positions.position: A military phrase and a challenge to battle: throw yourselves into a posture of defence and summon your idols, with a warning that the verse has no particular relation to the day of judgment or the hour of death.
Either sense will stand, feeble worms mustering against the mighty God, or a serious exhortation to meet the Lord by humiliation, repentance and reformation.
Leans to repentance, since the next chapter exhorts to it and sets out hope, the prophets always moderating the asperity of their doctrine after threatening destruction.

debates.question: Is the created thing in the doxology the wind or the soul of man?

positions.position: More probably the soul of man, since it agrees with the clause that follows, though both may be intended.
The wind, one word covering wind and spirit alike in Hebrew as in Greek, which makes the transition to the next clause natural.

outliers.claim: Records that the Greek version rendered the clause as declaring to man his Christ, through a misunderstanding of the original.
Rules out reading the threat backward over the chastisements just listed, since the formula always introduces what is about to happen and the future verb forbids it.

themes: Therefore thus will I do unto thee, O Israel: and because I will do this unto thee, prepare to meet thy God, O Israel.

For, lo, he that formeth the mountains, and createth the wind, and declareth unto man what is his thought, that maketh the morning darkness, and treadeth upon the high places of the earth, The Lord, The God of hosts, is his name.
